findings.title: Every row of the navigation drawer is unlabelled in the accessibility tree
findings.observed: All five drawer rows — account, games, places, settings, donate — are actionable containers that expose no accessible name, even though each renders visible text on screen. Two icon-only controls on the Explore feed (the bookmark and share buttons on the featured card) are unlabelled the same way.
findings.evidence: ux-03-more.json UX-001…UX-005 (ids main_drawer_account_container, _games_hub_, _places_, _settings_, _donate_); ux-01-feed.json UX-001–UX-002 at bounds [743,1064,869,1190] and [880,1064,1006,1190]; screens/03-more.png, screens/01-feed.png.
findings.steps: cold launch → More → read the accessibility tree; then Home → read the featured card
findings.expected: Each actionable row announces its own name. Read this as SUSPECTED, not proven: the snapshot folds child text into the nearest clickable ancestor, so the visible labels may be attached to a parent rather than genuinely missing. TalkBack is the only test that settles it.
findings.emulatorCaveat: no — the accessibility tree is the same surface TalkBack reads on a device
findings.falsePositiveIf: the snapshot folded each row's visible text into a clickable ancestor, so the name exists but is attached higher up the tree
findings.retest: enable TalkBack, swipe through the drawer, and confirm each row is announced by name

findings.title: The binary under review is signed by F-Droid, not by Wikimedia
findings.observed: The installed APK verifies cleanly (v1+v2+v3) but its certificate is CN=FDroid, O=fdroid.org — this is F-Droid's rebuild, not the artifact Google Play ships.
findings.evidence: apkscan.json signer.signerDN; pkgdiag.json reports installer '(none — sideloaded or preinstalled)'.
findings.steps: pull the installed APK → apkscan.py report
findings.expected: A signature that verifies proves the file was not altered after signing; it says nothing about who the signer is. Compare the certificate against a fingerprint you trust before calling this 'the Wikipedia app'.
findings.falsePositiveIf: you intended to review the F-Droid redistribution rather than the Play build
findings.retest: pull the Play build and compare its certificate SHA-256 against Wikimedia's published fingerprint

findings.title: Store and device disagree on the version under review
findings.observed: The Play listing advertises 50600-r-2026-07-28 while the device runs 50598-r-2026-07-13, so store-side numbers in this report describe a slightly newer build than the one measured.
findings.expected: Any comparison between store metrics and on-device behaviour should name both versions rather than implying a single build.
findings.falsePositiveIf: the listing was mid-rollout and the store version had not propagated
findings.retest: re-read both after the next store update and confirm they converge

findings.title: Jank rate reads poor, but the sample is far too small to act on
findings.observed: gfxinfo reported 13 janky frames out of 31 (41.9%) across the short tab-to-tab drive, which the thresholds score as 'poor'. The p90 frame time of 2.3 s is dominated by first-draw work, not steady-state scrolling.
findings.expected: A 31-frame window on an emulator is a smoke signal, not a measurement. Re-run on physical hardware over a scripted scroll before treating this as a regression.
findings.emulatorCaveat: yes — emulator rendering is not device-grade, and the window is tiny
findings.falsePositiveIf: the 31-frame window is dominated by first-draw work rather than steady-state scrolling — which it is
findings.retest: scripted 30-second scroll on physical hardware, gfxinfo reset first, several hundred frames

findings.title: Analytics endpoint dominates the app's network chatter
findings.observed: During the capture, intake-analytics.wikimedia.org drew 138 DNS lookups — an order of magnitude more than the content hosts en.wikipedia.org (10) and meta.wikimedia.org (4) — and its own TLS SNI confirms the app reached it directly.
findings.evidence: hosts.json dnsQueries and tlsServerNames; 1,479 packets captured, stats.complete true.
findings.steps: nettrace.py capture start → drive → capture stop → hosts
findings.expected: Worth confirming that beacon rate is intentional. The capture is device-wide, so the Google Play hosts in the same list belong to the OS, not to this app.
findings.falsePositiveIf: the lookups are retries against a single failing resolver rather than distinct beacons
findings.retest: capture again with an idle baseline subtracted and count TLS sessions, not DNS lookups

findings.title: System dialogs interrupted the crawl twice and had to be discarded
findings.observed: A Google Play purchase-verification dialog and, later, an external browser sign-in screen took the foreground mid-crawl. Two captured screens were of those overlays rather than of Wikipedia, and were re-taken; the browser frames were destroyed because they carried a real account address.
findings.evidence: Re-captured screens/03-more.png and screens/04-saved.png; the discarded frames are not in this report.
findings.expected: A crawl must check the foreground package every step (uia.py app current) and treat a change as an event, not as app content. Anything captured off-app is evidence about the device, not the app, and may contain personal data.
findings.emulatorCaveat: yes — a shared test device accumulates these prompts; a clean snapshot avoids them
findings.retest: re-run from a clean AVD snapshot with no Play prompts pending

findings.title: Layout holds across every configuration swept
findings.observed: All five cells passed with no crash, ANR or process death: baseline 411x914dp, a 320dp compact phone, landscape, an 840dp tablet width, and 200% font scale.
findings.evidence: matrix.json — verdict pass, 0 hard failures across 5 cells, device restored.
findings.expected: This is a pass, and worth stating: a review that only reports problems cannot show what it checked.
findings.falsePositiveIf: wm size/density resize one emulator's logical display — they do not reproduce a real tablet's aspect ratio, a hinge, a cutout you did not enable, or a vendor skin
findings.retest: repeat on a purpose-built tablet AVD and on physical hardware
findings.emulatorCaveat: yes — resize fidelity is limited, see the matrix section

findings.title: Every exported entry point is reachable from any other app, and none of them crashed
findings.observed: Firing all 13 exported components from outside: 14 probes launched, 2 services were refused by the platform (BIND_REMOTEVIEWS, BIND_JOB_SERVICE), 1 alias did not resolve, and nothing crashed. The https deep link opens PageActivity for any caller.
findings.evidence: intents.json — launched 14, denied 2, not-found 1; no FATAL EXCEPTION in the crash buffer for any probe.
findings.steps: apkscan.py report base.apk --json → intentprobe.py run org.wikipedia --go
findings.expected: This is what a browser-handling reader app should look like: the reachable surface is content display, and the privileged pieces are permission-gated. Reachability alone is not a defect.
findings.falsePositiveIf: a launch only proves the component started — none of these were followed into their post-launch state to see whether any skipped a gate
findings.retest: drive each launched component with android-ui-driver and check whether it reaches a state the normal path gates

limits: Four top-level screens on one device, one locale and one Android version — this is a shape-of-the-app pass, not a release sign-off.
The reviewed artifact is F-Droid's rebuild of 50598; conclusions do not transfer to the Play build without re-running against it.
No account was used, so every logged-in surface of the app is unreviewed.
Crash buffers were not cleared before the run, so 'no crashes' means none left in the ring buffer, not none ever.
Screenshots in this report were reviewed for personal data before publication; one screen was discarded rather than redacted.
